Impetigo and Ecthyma

Impetigo is a superficial skin infection that rarely causes systemic symptoms. Ecthyma is a skin infection characterized by crusted sores beneath which ulcers form. It is a deep form of impetigo, as the same bacteria causing the infection are involved. Ecthyma causes deeper erosions of the skin into the dermis.

Gram stain and culture of the pus or exudates from skin lesions of impetigo and ecthyma are recommended to help identify whether Staphylococcus aureus and/or beta-hemolytic Streptococcus is the cause.

Bullous and non-bullous impetigo can be treated with oral or topical antimicrobials, but oral therapy is recommended for patients with numerous lesions or in outbreaks affecting several people to help decrease transmission of infection. Treatment for ecthyma should be an oral antimicrobial.

Therapy:
## Inpatient

## Treatment for impetigo with few lesions

Mupirocin ointment to affected area q8h for 5 days ($) [M]

## Treatment for ecthyma and for impetigo with numerous lesions or whose symptoms have not responded to topical treatment

Treat orally for 7 days

## Alternative for penicillin allergy

Doxycycline 100MG PO q12h ($) [DI]

## IF MRSA confirmed or suspected:

Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) [R,DI]
Doxycycline 100MG PO q12h ($) [DI]

## Outpatient

## Treatment for impetigo with few lesions

Mupirocin ointment to affected area TID for 5 days ($) [M]
Non-VA order for above

## Treatment for ecthyma and for impetigo with numerous lesions or whose symptoms have not responded to topical treatment

Treat orally for 7 days
Non-VA order for above

## Alternative for penicillin allergy
